intelligence.human_view: A builder who hands over a half-finished room for the owner to judge is not saving time — he is spending the owner's attention, which is the one thing the machine exists to save. So the gate moves: nothing comes back until it is a ten, and he drives it there himself. The mechanic keeps the engine running behind the wall; the interface master owns everything he sees. And the ten is provable on the path he walks himself — walkthrough, certificate, agreement, into the Hub — not claimed by a round. The Factory proved it the same way: one click, a real live page, byte-identical to the build — the first real one-click build ever proven, after the only end-to-end verdict before it said "No build ever lands."
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you're building a tower for Dad, and you don't show it to him until every brick is perfect — a ten! You keep working on it yourself until it's a ten, and then you show him. And the machine that builds the tower is fixed now — you press one button, and a real tower appears, exactly like the picture. And the lady's voice on the page is her real voice now, not a robot voice.
intelligence.grandma_view: Dear, you don't show him the work, dear, until it's a ten, dear — you keep driving it yourself, dear, until it's perfect, dear. And the machine that builds it is fixed now, dear — one button, and a real page appears, dear, just like the picture, dear. And the lady's voice is her real voice now, dear, not a robot, dear.
intelligence.naya_view: WORK COMES BACK ONLY WHEN IT IS A TEN. NOTHING IS SENT BACK TO HIM BEFORE THAT — HE KEEPS DRIVING UNTIL IT HITS TEN. A BUILD COUNTS ONLY WHEN ONE CLICK ENDS ON A REAL LIVE PAGE, BYTE-IDENTICAL TO THE BUILD. DECIDE, DECLARE, BECOME.
